title: Determine the sharp odd denominator for noise-optimal four-qubit Clifford decoding
body:
For the normalized four-qubit Clifford tensor map at width 13, the least common odd denominator among all exact Gaussian-rational left inverses attaining the optimal Euclidean operator norm is **470,624,175**. At every width f ≥ 13 the required odd denominator is the reduced numerator of the smallest Gram eigenvalue. With dyadic coefficients on a 2⁻ˢ grid, the optimal excess in **squared** noise norm is Θ_f(4⁻ˢ).

A primitive vector in the least eigenspace proves necessity. One correction using the reciprocal least eigenvalue, followed by dyadic corrections supported away from the bottom eigenspace, proves attainment. The proof also shows why both Gram endpoints carry from width 4k−1 to 4k. It builds on the splitting in #7799, Ali Romman's spectra and canonical obstruction in #7770, #7772, #7788, #7789 and #7792, and Nick Petalas's projection data from #7747.

The replay checks 81 width-13 levels, 1,701 projected neutral-sector equalities, exact precision-grid examples, and independent dense calculations on the 24-element one-qubit alphabet. The constants in the precision result depend on the fixed matrix. A practical compact norm-optimal decoder and the exact denominator of the canonical inverse itself remain open.
